activities.title: A longer story
activities.text: Choose a story with more pages and fewer pictures. Take turns reading a page each.

activities.title: Pictures in the mind
activities.text: After a page, close the book and ask your child to describe what they see in their mind: the place, the people, the weather.

activities.title: One step up
activities.text: Pick a book a little harder than usual. Let your child read the first page to you, and help only when asked.

activities.title: Make your own ending
activities.text: Stop before the end of a story and ask your child how they think it ends. Then read on together and compare.

activities.title: Family reader
activities.text: Ask your child to read a short story or notice aloud to the family, then tell everyone what it was about.

activities.title: Sound hunt
activities.text: Pick a sound from a word your child found hard today, like the 'ch' in 'chose'. Find three things at home or at the market that start with that sound.

activities.title: Word builder
activities.text: Write a word from the story that was hard today. Cover the end, read the first part together, then uncover the rest and read the whole word.

activities.title: Word families
activities.text: Write words that end the same way, like hat, cat and mat. Read them together, then make up a funny sentence that uses them.

activities.title: Talk about class-level stories
activities.text: Keep reading stories at your child's class level aloud to them and ask what happened and why. Understanding is a strength, so keep it growing.

activities.title: Word cards
activities.text: Write five words your child paused on today on small cards. Read them together each day, and put a card away once the word feels easy.

activities.title: Chunk long words
activities.text: Show how a long word breaks into parts, like 'to-ge-ther'. Clap the parts together, then read the whole word.

activities.title: Listen and learn
activities.text: Read class-level books aloud to your child, or play an audio story, and talk about them. Your child understands a lot when listening, so keep that going while their word reading grows.

activities.title: Easy-to-sound-out books
activities.text: Choose short books with simple, regular words. Let your child read each one more than once; reading it again builds speed.

activities.title: Finger along
activities.text: Let your child point under each word while reading slowly. For a hard word, point to each sound in turn.

activities.title: Stop and ask why
activities.text: While reading together, stop every few sentences and ask 'Why do you think that happened?' Let your child answer before you read on.

activities.title: Word talk
activities.text: Pick two new words from a story. Talk about what they mean, and use each one in a sentence about your day.

activities.title: Read aloud and discuss
activities.text: Read a story aloud to your child, then talk about it together: who was in it, what problem they had, and how it was solved.

activities.title: Who is 'he'?
activities.text: When a story says 'he', 'she' or 'they', pause and ask your child who it means.

activities.title: Feelings detective
activities.text: Ask how a character feels, and what in the story tells you so.

activities.title: Tell it back
activities.text: After a story, ask your child to tell it to someone else in the family in their own words.

activities.title: Echo reading
activities.text: Read one sentence with lots of expression, then let your child read the same sentence back, copying how you said it.

activities.title: Everyday words
activities.text: Practise five common words a week, like 'the', 'went' and 'said'. Spot them together in books, on signs and on packets.

activities.title: Naming game
activities.text: At home or at the market, take turns naming things in a group, like fruits, colours or animals, and describing one of them.

activities.title: Picture talk
activities.text: Before reading, look at the pictures in a book together and talk about what might happen.

activities.title: One part at a time
activities.text: Read one short part of a story, then ask your child to tell you what happened in it before you read the next part.

activities.title: Read, then tell
activities.text: Your child reads a short page alone, then tells you about it. If a part is hard to remember, read it again together and talk it through.

activities.title: Question maker
activities.text: After reading, your child asks you a question about the story. Answer it, then swap.

activities.title: Slow and steady
activities.text: Ask your child to read a page slowly and pause at each full stop to think about what it said.

activities.title: Label hunt
activities.text: On errands, read labels, signs and packets together, and ask your child what each one tells you.

activities.title: First, next, last
activities.text: After a story, ask your child what happened first, what happened next, and how it ended.
